text:
Noah Ostlund has made the jump this season. The 22-year-old Swede is playing 18:56 a night, up from 13:58 last season, and he's on the ice for 72% of Buffalo's power-play chances after seeing 15% a year ago. The Sabres' own video put Lindy Ruff's verdict in the title: "He's A Coach's Dream."

The production has followed the role: 10 points in 17 games, and his own chances have more than doubled, to 1.02 expected goals per 60 from 0.45. If anything he's been a little unlucky. He's shooting 9.3% against a league norm around 13%, and the Sabres have scored about two fewer goals than their chances deserved with him out there.

How he plays is the fun part. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 67% of his shots coming off the rush last season and 20% of his setups going across the royal road, almost three times a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey had him as a defensive plus, too. Our range for his season: about 51 points, with room to 64. Seventeen games is still early, but this looks like a role, not a heater.
headline: Noah Ostlund has graduated to the big minutes
